content.value_statement: Teachers need AI activities that build skill instead of replacing practice. This skill structures lessons where students use AI, critique outputs, and verify learning independently.
actual_capabilities: Applies the Three Roles Framework to AI-integrated programming lessons.
Defines foundation, AI-assisted, and independent verification phases.
Provides prompt design guidance for context, task, constraints, and output format.
Includes templates for AI lesson planning and prompt quality review.
Offers scripts to assess AI integration balance and prompt quality.
Supports ethical reflection on attribution, independence, and responsible AI use.
limitations: Focused on AI-integrated programming education, not general curriculum design.
Requires instructors to adapt examples to their course level and policies.
Does not replace assessment design, accreditation review, or institutional approval.
Scripts analyze local lesson materials but do not prove student learning outcomes.

use_cases.title: Plan AI-Supported Coding Lessons
use_cases.description: Create lessons that combine manual practice, AI collaboration, and AI-free verification.

use_cases.title: Teach Prompt Quality
use_cases.description: Guide learners to write prompts with clear context, constraints, examples, and verification criteria.

use_cases.title: Review Responsible AI Use
use_cases.description: Add reflection, attribution, and independence checks to AI-assisted development workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Beginner Lesson
prompt_templates.scenario: A teacher is introducing AI assistance for the first time.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a 60-minute beginner programming lesson that uses AI only after students practice the core skill manually. Include one AI-free checkpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Balance AI Collaboration
prompt_templates.scenario: An instructor wants a lesson with structured AI use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a lesson plan using foundation, AI-assisted exploration, and independent verification phases. Set a clear percentage balance for each phase.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Student Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Students need better prompts for coding support.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this student prompt for context, task clarity, constraints, output format, and testable criteria. Suggest a stronger learning-focused version.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full AI Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: A course team is reviewing an advanced AI-assisted project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this AI-assisted project workflow for the Three Roles Framework, convergence loops, ethical disclosure, and independent capability checks.

output_examples.input: Request: Create a Python functions lesson for beginners with limited AI use.
output: A phased lesson with manual syntax practice before AI assistance.
A guided AI exploration task for alternative examples and test cases.
An independent checkpoint where students explain and write functions without AI.

output_examples.input: Request: Review whether a prompt helps students learn debugging.
output: Feedback on missing context, weak task wording, and absent verification criteria.
A revised prompt that asks for diagnosis, explanation, and student-led testing.
Reflection questions that check whether students understand the fix.

output_examples.input: Request: Add responsible AI practices to a coding assignment.
output: A log format for prompts, outputs, decisions, and learning notes.
An AI-free demonstration task to verify independent capability.

best_practices: Protect foundational practice before introducing AI assistance.
Require students to verify, explain, and adapt AI-generated suggestions.
Document AI use with prompts, outputs, decisions, and learning reflections.
anti_patterns: Letting AI complete the full task before students understand the core concept.
Assessing only final output without reviewing student reasoning and verification.
Using vague prompts that omit context, constraints, examples, and expected results.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI-integrated programming lessons with clear collaboration, verification, and reflection stages.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this only for beginner students?
faq.answer: No. It includes guidance for beginner, intermediate, and advanced AI collaboration levels.

faq.question: Does it generate complete course curricula?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on AI-integrated lessons, prompt activities, and verification practices.

faq.question: How does it prevent over-reliance on AI?
faq.answer: It uses foundation phases, AI-free checkpoints, reflection prompts, and independent demonstrations.

faq.question: Can it check prompt quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes local guidance and a validator script for clarity, context, task, and testability.
